labs.analysis:
Three things need to happen before I can do useful clinical work with you. They're not parallel blockers — they form a sequence, and the sequence matters.

The first is the protein escalation. Your intake is currently averaging 151.6 g/day against an actual average of 121.4 g/day as recently as the broader trend. More importantly, the September 16th gate was explicit: kidney function verification before further escalation. That gate exists because at sustained caloric restriction with high protein load, GFR and creatinine tell me whether your kidneys are handling the nitrogen burden appropriately. The clinical frame here is directional — I'm recommending we hold escalation at current levels until we have that kidney function data, not because I'm certain there's a problem, but because the pretest probability of elevated creatinine or BUN is non-trivial at your current intake level, your starting body weight, and 174 days since the last CMP. I can't clear this without the data. The nutrition target is 190 g/day — I want you there as much as anyone — but the path there runs through a metabolic panel, not around it.

The second is the symptom baseline. Fatigue score (1–10) and cold tolerance, collected today. I've asked for this across 12 days of requests, and I want to explain why it's not optional: at 1,515 kcal/day sustained restriction, the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis will eventually respond. T3 conversion drops as the body defends against perceived caloric deficit — this is a documented adaptive response, not a hypothesis. When I get the next TSH, free T3, and free T4 values, the only way I can distinguish pre-existing hypothyroid tendency from protocol-induced downregulation is by knowing your symptom state *before* the draw. Without a baseline, the panel becomes clinically ambiguous. Two numbers, collected today, make the next thyroid result interpretable. Without them, I'm reading smoke with no prior knowledge of whether there was a fire already burning.

On the wearable picture: the night of 2026-09-24 showed a 99% recovery score, HRV of 56.8 ms, and resting HR of 52 bpm — directionally positive, and the EWMA trends across the past three weeks point the same way. The physical coach has already covered the statistical framing on these, and I'll defer to that analysis on the autocorrelation question. My angle is simpler: these signals are running 174 days without a biochemical anchor. The next panel — whenever it happens — will either confirm that the wearable trends reflect genuine physiological adaptation, or flag that they're moving against a backdrop of subclinical inflammation, metabolic stress, or thyroid suppression we haven't measured. Until then, the directional story is plausible. It is not confirmed.

Two asks this cycle: hold protein at current levels, and send me a fatigue score and cold tolerance rating today.

Those are three separate hypotheses and they require separate data streams to distinguish.
